searches.query: Christoph Schönnenbeck parabolic induction Hecke algebras dissertation alternative full text
searches.outcome: Found the author-hosted 2016 master thesis, plus independent full-text treatments by Geck, Lusztig and Mathas; these accessible treatments and complete local proofs cover every HH-13 item.

alternatives.argument: The item directly defines H_J as the R-span of the existing standard-basis elements T_u for u in W_J and defines induction by the published balanced module tensor product. Its declared justifier thm-hh-parabolic-hecke-freeness-and-induced-bases proves the span is a subalgebra and the restricted Hecke map is injective; this supplies the missing local construction argument without relying on the failed fetch.

The item proof establishes H_J closure and restricted-presentation injection in steps 1.1-1.2. Steps 2.1-2.2 prove both module decompositions by unique minimal-coset factorization, length-additive reduced products and independence in the standard basis. Step 3.1 identifies the balanced tensor product with a direct sum of copies of M, and step 4.1 proves the induction-restriction Hom bijection by inverse formulas.

The item defines tau as the identity coefficient in the unique standard-basis expansion and defines symmetry and perfectness over R explicitly. Its declared justifier thm-hh-canonical-hecke-trace-is-symmetric-and-perfect proves the requested properties; no field-vector-space duality is used.

The item proof checks self-adjointness of each left length operator on every two-element orbit (step 1.1), reverses reduced words to obtain P_x^t=P_(x^-1) (step 2.1), computes tau(T_xT_y)=delta_(x^-1,y) (step 3.1), identifies the coordinate dual basis to prove the R-module isomorphism (step 4.1), and transports the permutation Gram matrix through arbitrary commutative base change (step 5.1).
